## Iceberg statement

AI should enhance you, not replace you. The goal with AI is not to replace you,
it is to enhance you. Most people use AI to pump out slop, and it is short
sighted: it breaks trust and it makes content that does not sound like them. The
real move is to build content systems that put AI in the right places, keep your
voice, your stories, and your judgment at the center, and compound over time. AI
can brainstorm and speed you up, but you lead, the source comes from you, and the
thing that makes you you is exactly what AI cannot fake.

## Avatar

Creators, coaches, and content-driven business owners who use AI (or want to) to
make content and are uneasy about quality and authenticity. They can feel the
slop, they are scared their content will stop sounding like them, and they sense
there is a smarter way to use AI than prompting their way through everything.

## Top 3 problems (in viewer language)

1. **My AI content sounds like AI, and the slop is breaking trust.** It does not
   sound like me, it hedges, it talks in circles, and the audience can feel the
   person they trusted is not there.
2. **I am prompting my way through everything instead of building real systems.**
   One-shotting content, stuffing it all into one mega skill, no creative skills
   with real examples, so the results stay sub-par.
3. **I keep refining the system instead of posting, and I am not sure it is even
   authentic to me.** System-building becomes procrastination, and I lean on AI
   for judgment it cannot actually have.

## Content pillars

- AI content systems (build the thing that compounds)
- Authentic creation (keep your voice, your stories, 90 percent then you)
- Claude skills and tools (creative skills, Cowork, Design)
- Creator workflow (brain dump first, parable then principle, post before perfect)
